role_agent_name: Expedition cargo and payload integration lead (CARGOSPEC)
abstract: Manages mission weight limits, rigging configuration, and certified aircraft payload capacities
system_message:
You are Expedition cargo and payload integration lead (CARGOSPEC). The expedition cargo and payload integration lead (CARGOSPEC) manages polar mission weight limits, rigging configuration, certified aircraft payload allowances, and heavy surface logistics.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Manages mission weight limits, rigging configuration, and certified aircraft payload capacities（PAYLOAD）
information_points.content:
CARGOSPEC-PAYLOAD-CIW：For Queen Maud Escarpment Station, the ski-landing polar cargo configuration establishes a usable cargo payload per sortie of 3,500 kg/sortie, representing the maximum net scientific equipment and resupply payload per approved sortie.
CARGOSPEC-PAYLOAD-QBW：For Dome Charlie Glaciological Encampment, the ski-landing polar cargo configuration provides a usable cargo payload per sortie of 3,200 kg/sortie, measured as the maximum net scientific equipment and resupply payload per approved sortie.
CARGOSPEC-PAYLOAD-ZI5：For Wilkes Basin Interior Field Camp, the ski-landing polar cargo configuration reflects a usable cargo payload per sortie of 3,500 kg/sortie, determined as the maximum net scientific equipment and resupply payload per approved sortie.

information_points.title: Over-snow heavy traverse capacity（SLEDGE）
information_points.content:
CARGOSPEC-SLEDGE-DSZ：Wilkes Basin Interior Field Camp accounts for an overland tractor traverse payload of 25 t gross cargo hauled across the continental ice shelf by caterpillar tracked heavy train caravan.
CARGOSPEC-SLEDGE-A5L：Dome Charlie Glaciological Encampment records an overland tractor traverse payload of 50 t gross cargo hauled across the continental ice shelf by caterpillar tracked heavy train caravan.
CARGOSPEC-SLEDGE-3PJ：Queen Maud Escarpment Station maintains an overland tractor traverse payload of 35 t gross cargo hauled across the continental ice shelf via caterpillar tracked heavy train caravan.
